name: Porter

modes.label: Native service
modes.note: Hardware and complete resource tariff unverified.

modes.label: Porter Sandboxes (AWS, in your own account)
modes.note: Container sandboxes on a Karpenter node group of local-NVMe EC2 instances in the customer's AWS account. The Porter platform fee ($0.019/vCPU-h + $0.009/GB-h on requested resources) presumably applies, but no sandbox-specific pricing is published. EC2 cost is extra. Warm pods 'reserve their CPU and memory on the sandbox node group even while idle', so idle warm-pool capacity costs EC2 money. Default Max CPU is 20 cores per sandbox node group (queued beyond that; raise it self-serve). Max single sandbox 256 cores / 1 TB. Warm-pool pod size 0.1–16 CPU, 64 MiB–32 GiB. TTL is optional. Azure/GCP are beta on request.

plans.name: Standard
plans.note: Metered: $13/vCPU-month ($0.019/h) + $6/GB-RAM-month ($0.009/h) on requested app resources, prorated to the minute. Underlying cloud not included.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Volume discount above 40 vCPU / 80 GB RAM. Adds premium support, advanced RBAC, SAML SSO, custom alerts and on-prem installation.

caveats: Platform fee only: requested vCPU $0.019/h, memory $0.009/GB-h, minute prorated. Website monthly $13/$6 are rounded illustrative numbers. Underlying AWS/Azure/GCP NOT included; over 40vCPU/80GB negotiated discounts. Nonprofit 50% off conditional. Do not rank software surcharge as all-in compute.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
Startup deal through investors (e.g. Y Combinator, a16z speedrun) or by application. Terms are not public. Cloud credits can pay the underlying AWS/Azure/GCP bill.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Unlike a sandbox's own filesystem, which is discarded when the sandbox exits, a volume lives independently and keeps its contents across sandboxes.
snapshot_auto.note: Porter Sandboxes (AWS/EKS, in your own account) have no pause/sleep; the sandbox filesystem is discarded on exit/TTL. Only explicit snapshots or volumes persist state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures a running sandbox's filesystem so you can start new sandboxes from it later, with the same files in place.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem only: 'A snapshot holds files only, not running processes or mounted volumes'. Sandbox must be running; capture pauses it for a few ms. New sandboxes boot from it (porter.snapshots.create / porter sandbox create --from-snapshot) -> fork/template, no memory.

harness_api.quote: Bake your harness into a custom image, inject the model API key at create time, and run it as the sandbox's main process.
harness_api.note: Only generic create/exec/logs APIs; running an agent is DIY via custom image. (Porter's MCP server and dashboard DevOps Agent operate Porter itself, not a harness in a sandbox.)

egress_allowlist.quote: Pass `egress` when creating a sandbox and it can only reach the destinations it lists; all other outbound traffic is blocked. Enforcement happens transparently at the network layer, so any protocol and client works without proxy configuration.
egress_allowlist.note: Entries: exact hostname, *.wildcard, IP, CIDR, or k8s Service. 'An empty list denies all egress.' Requires cluster setting 'Enforce egress allowlists' (network policy on sandbox nodes). Default isolation also blocks private ranges, metadata endpoint, other pods.

ingress_rules.quote: `public` or `private`: whether the sandbox is served publicly or inside your VPC when the cluster has both configured.
ingress_rules.note: A sandbox exposes nothing unless `networking` lists a port; public (internet LB) vs private (internal LB, VPC only) vs `internal: true` (cluster-internal address only). No per-URL auth tokens documented. Porter apps additionally support AWS ALB/WAF IP allowlisting.

secret_proxy.quote: Instead of passing variables one at a time, you can inject an entire [environment group](/applications/configure/environment-groups) from the cluster at create time.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are env vars / env groups (incl. Doppler/Infisical-synced) placed inside the sandbox; docs recommend injecting the model API key as an env var. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes are persistent storage you can mount into Porter Sandboxes.
volume_attach.note: Disk volumes (cluster disks) and object volumes (S3 bucket via Mountpoint for S3, AWS only), mounted at launch via volume_mounts; files readable/writable from outside via SDK/CLI/dashboard.

volume_shared.quote: Any number of sandboxes can mount the same object volume at once, on any sandbox cluster.
volume_shared.note: Object (S3) volumes: read-write / read-only / write-only-new-files, no in-place edits or appends. Disk volumes: concurrent multi-sandbox mounts only if 'the cluster to back sandbox volumes with shared storage; without it, a volume attaches to one sandbox at a time.' Porter apps (non-sandbox) get EFS shared RW disks.
